examples.en: I practiced with a friend at the table tennis table.

examples.ko: 학교 체육관에 탁구대가 네 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are four table tennis tables in the school gym.
I folded the table tennis table and stood it against the wall.
I'm looking into buying a new table tennis table.
The ball fell on the table tennis table.
Shall we play a game at our table?

explain: 탁구를 치는 '대(판)'를 말하고, 탁구를 하는 장소는 '탁구장'이라고 해서 구별해요. 보통 '탁구를 치다'라고 말해요. 가운데 있는 그물은 '네트'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The ball fell onto the table-tennis table.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위'와 함께 써서 탁구대의 판 부분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with '위' to mean the playing surface.

phrases.en: We set up a new ping-pong table in the gym.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탁구대를 설치하거나 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when setting up or placing a table.
phrases.en_equiv: to set up a ping-pong table

phrases.en: There is a net in the middle of the ping-pong table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탁구대의 부품을 말할 때 이렇게 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name a part belonging to the table.

explain_en: This is the table itself, while the place for playing is called '탁구장', so keep them apart. People normally say '탁구를 치다'. The net in the middle is called '네트'.

examples.en: At karaoke, my friend shook the tambourine.
The kindergarten kids sang while hitting tambourines.

examples.ko: 탬버린 소리가 신나서 저절로 박수가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The tambourine sound was so lively that I started clapping.
I took charge of the tambourine in the band.

examples.ko: 탬버린은 박자에 맞춰 치면 훨씬 재미있어요.
examples.en: A tambourine is much more fun when you hit it in time with the beat.
An old tambourine turned up in the drawer.

explain: '탬버린'은 한국에서 노래방에 꼭 있는 도구라서 악기보다 '분위기를 띄우는 물건'으로 더 많이 알려졌어요. '탬버린을 치다', '탬버린을 흔들다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: We clapped along with the sound of the tambourine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기가 내는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the sound the instrument makes.

phrases.en: I danced holding a tambourine at karaoke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손에 들고 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe holding it in your hand.

phrases.en: We played the tambourine in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기로 쓴다는 뜻이라서 음악 수업 이야기에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Treats it as an instrument, fitting for music class.

explain_en: '탬버린' is found in almost every Korean karaoke room, so it is known more as a party-livening prop than as an instrument. People say '탬버린을 치다' or '탬버린을 흔들다'.

examples.ko: 저는 턱걸이를 열 개 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can do ten chin-ups.
I did chin-ups on the bar in the park.
Chin-ups are good exercise for the arms and back.

examples.ko: 턱걸이가 너무 어려워서 한 개도 못 해요.
examples.en: Chin-ups are so hard that I can't do even one.
I'm practicing chin-ups a little every day.
My shoulder hurt while I was doing chin-ups.

explain: 철봉을 잡고 몸을 끌어올려 턱이 철봉 위로 오게 하는 운동이에요. 바닥에서 하는 '팔굽혀펴기'와 구별해요. 보통 '턱걸이를 하다'라고 말해요. 아래처럼 겨우 해냈다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: My score was borderline, but I just barely passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기준에 겨우 맞춰 간신히 통과한다는 뜻이에요. 시험, 입학, 심사 같은 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means just barely meeting the cutoff. Used for exams, admissions and screenings.

explain_en: It is the exercise of pulling yourself up on a bar until your chin is over it. Do not mix it up with '팔굽혀펴기' (push-ups), done on the floor. It is normally said as '턱걸이를 하다'. It is also used to mean barely managing something, as shown below.

examples.en: My older brother is learning hapkido.
At the hapkido dojang we practiced how to fall first.
Hapkido is a sport that uses the opponent's force.
I went to the gym to see a hapkido demonstration.
I go to hapkido class every weekend.
How are hapkido and taekwondo different?

explain: 한국에는 태권도, 합기도, 검도, 유도처럼 '-도'로 끝나는 무술 이름이 많아요. 합기도는 상대를 잡고 던지는 기술이 많아서 발차기가 중심인 태권도와 느낌이 달라요. '합기도를 하다/배우다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I have done hapkido since I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배우다'보다 오래 운동해 왔다는 느낌으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared with 배우다, it can suggest practicing for a long time.

phrases.en: The hapkido master corrected my posture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무술을 가르치는 선생님을 높여 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful term for a martial arts instructor.

phrases.en: There is a hapkido class every Saturday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 시간이나 수업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about class times.

explain_en: Many Korean martial arts end in '-도', such as 태권도, 합기도, 검도 and 유도. Hapkido has many grabbing and throwing techniques, so it feels different from taekwondo, which centers on kicks. You say '합기도를 하다/배우다'.

examples.ko: 아빠가 설거지를 하면서 노래를 흥얼흥얼 불러요.
examples.en: Dad hums a song while doing the dishes.

examples.ko: 길을 걷다가 저도 모르게 흥얼흥얼 따라 불렀어요.
examples.en: While walking, I found myself humming along without realizing it.
He cleaned his room, humming a tune.
I could hear someone humming while they showered.

examples.ko: 어머니가 흥얼흥얼 옛 노래를 부르며 요리하세요.
examples.en: My mother cooks while humming an old song.

examples.ko: 운전하면서 라디오 노래를 흥얼흥얼 따라 했어요.
examples.en: I hummed along to the radio while driving.

explain: 기분이 좋거나 무심코 작은 소리로 노래를 부르는 모습이에요. 보통 '노래를 흥얼흥얼 부르다'처럼 쓰고, 동사로는 '흥얼거리다'를 더 많이 말해요. 크게 노래하는 것이 아니라 혼자 중얼거리듯 부르는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I hum a song while showering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흥얼흥얼'의 동사형으로 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '흥얼흥얼', used more in daily speech.

phrases.en: He must be in a good mood, humming a tune.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분 좋을 때 혼자 작게 부르는 콧노래를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Quiet humming that one does alone when in a good mood.

phrases.en: I hummed along to the commercial jingle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들은 노래를 작은 소리로 따라 부르는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Quietly following along with a song you heard.

explain_en: It describes softly singing to yourself, usually when you are in a good mood or without thinking. It is typically used as in '노래를 흥얼흥얼 부르다', and as a verb people more often say '흥얼거리다'. It is not full-voiced singing but more like singing under your breath.

examples.ko: 시골 길에서 당나귀가 짐을 끌고 있었어요.
examples.en: A donkey was pulling a load on a country road.
The kids rode a donkey and took photos.
A donkey is smaller in body than a horse.

examples.ko: 동화 속 당나귀에게 이름을 붙여 줬어요.
examples.en: I gave the donkey in the fairy tale a name.

examples.ko: 이솝 이야기에는 사자 가죽을 쓴 당나귀가 나와요.
examples.en: In Aesop's fables, there is a donkey wearing a lion's skin.
I have a friend who is stubborn like a donkey.

explain: '임금님 귀는 당나귀 귀'라는 옛이야기로 한국 사람에게 친숙한 동물이에요. 말보다 몸집이 작고 짐을 나르는 모습을 먼저 떠올려요. 한국 시골에서는 보기 어려워서 책이나 여행에서 만나는 동물이에요.

phrases.en: I rode a donkey on my trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당나귀 위에 올라타는 경험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the experience of riding on a donkey.

phrases.en: A donkey's ears are long and big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛이야기 '임금님 귀는 당나귀 귀'에서 많이 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard from the old tale 'The King Has Donkey Ears.'

phrases.en: There is one donkey in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물은 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with '마리.'

explain_en: Koreans know this animal from the old tale '임금님 귀는 당나귀 귀'. It is smaller than a horse, and people first picture it carrying loads. It is hard to see in the Korean countryside, so people meet it in books or on trips.

t90.ax: The kids rode a donkey and took photos.

en: to breed; to raise; to rear

examples.en: My grandfather raises chickens in the countryside.
They are raising cattle on this farm.
It is hard to raise large animals at home.

examples.ko: 동물원은 멸종 위기 동물을 사육해서 지켜요.
examples.en: Zoos protect endangered animals by breeding them.

examples.ko: 사육한 지 오 년 된 말이에요.
examples.en: It is a horse that has been raised for five years.

examples.ko: 좁은 곳에서 사육하면 동물이 스트레스를 받아요.
examples.en: If you raise animals in cramped places, they get stressed.

explain: '사육하다'는 농장이나 동물원에서 동물을 먹여 기르는 일이에요. 집에서 강아지나 고양이를 기를 때는 '키우다'가 자연스럽고, '사육하다'를 쓰면 가축처럼 느껴져요. 식물을 기를 때는 '재배하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 아버지는 소와 돼지 같은 가축을 사육해요.
phrases.en: My father raises livestock such as cows and pigs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가축과 함께 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing, used with livestock.

phrases.en: This farm is raising ducks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 기르고 있는 중이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is currently being raised.

phrases.en: We keep a puppy at our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반려동물에는 '사육하다' 대신 '키우다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 키우다 instead of 사육하다 for pets.

explain_en: Raising animals on land; formal, farming context. 사육하다 is feeding and raising animals on a farm or in a zoo. For a pet dog or cat at home, '키우다' is natural, and 사육하다 would make it sound like livestock. For plants use '재배하다'.

t90.ax: They are raising cattle on this farm.

examples.en: It's a blanket light as a feather, so it's warm and comfortable.
A single bird feather had fallen on the floor.

examples.ko: 새털이 빠진 자리에 새로 털이 나요.
examples.en: New feathers grow where the old ones fell out.

examples.ko: 새털로 만든 장식이 인형 머리에 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: A decoration made of feathers is stuck on the doll's head.

examples.ko: 아이가 새털을 주워 책 사이에 끼웠어요.
examples.en: The child picked up a feather and tucked it between the pages of a book.
Feathers are light, so the wind blows them away easily.

explain: 새의 가는 털을 말하는데, 큰 날개 깃털은 '깃털'이라고 더 자주 해요. 그래서 '새털'은 가볍고 부드러운 느낌을 말할 때 자주 어울려요.

phrases.example: 아직 시간은 새털같이 많으니까 서두르지 마세요.
phrases.en: We still have plenty of time, so don't rush.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주로 '날', '시간'과 함께 써서 앞으로 남은 날이 아주 많다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Usually used with '날' or '시간' to mean there are very many days or much time still ahead.

explain_en: It means a bird's fine feathers, while the larger wing feathers are more often called '깃털'. So '새털' fits best when you want to convey lightness or softness.

examples.en: I tried trout sashimi in Gangwon-do.
I went for a trout fishing experience.
Trout live in cold, clear water.
I caught a trout myself at the winter festival.
I squeezed lemon on the grilled trout and ate it.
My mother grilled a trout for me.

explain: 연어와 모양이 비슷하지만 송어는 주로 민물에서 길러 먹어요. 한국에서는 겨울 송어 축제와 '송어회'로 유명해요.

phrases.en: Trout sashimi is soft and nutty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 송어를 날것으로 먹는 음식이고, 송어를 먹는 가장 흔한 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Raw trout sashimi, the most common way trout is eaten.

phrases.en: A trout festival is held every winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울에 송어를 잡고 먹는 행사예요. 송어 이야기를 할 때 같이 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A winter event for catching and eating trout; it often comes up with this word.

phrases.en: The child caught one trout.
phrases.nuance_ko: 송어 한 마리를 낚거나 손으로 잡는 일을 말해요. 낚시 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means catching a trout by fishing or by hand; used when talking about fishing.

explain_en: It looks similar to salmon, but trout is mostly raised and eaten from fresh water. In Korea it is known for winter trout festivals and '송어회'.

examples.en: I saw an otter for the first time at the zoo.

examples.ko: 수달 한 마리가 물속에서 헤엄치고 있어요.
examples.en: An otter is swimming in the water.
Otters catch and eat fish.
In Korea, otters are a protected animal.
I got a cute otter doll as a present.
The otter is an animal that swims in clear rivers.

explain: 강과 하천에 사는 동물이에요. 바다에 사는 비슷한 동물은 '해달'이라고 불러서 서로 달라요. 한국에서는 천연기념물이라 뉴스에서 '수달 발견'처럼 나오기도 해요.

phrases.en: A baby otter plays next to its mom.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수달' 앞에 말을 붙여 새끼를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a word before 수달 to mean the young.

phrases.en: Otters live in this river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사는 곳을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for talking about habitat.

phrases.en: Sea otters live in the ocean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다에 사는 비슷한 동물이라 '수달'과 구별해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar sea-dwelling animal, distinct from 수달.

explain_en: An animal that lives in rivers and streams. The similar sea-dwelling animal is called '해달' (sea otter), so the two differ. In Korea it is a natural monument, so news sometimes reports '수달 발견' (otter sighted).

examples.en: When spring came, daffodils bloomed in the garden.

examples.ko: 노란 수선화 한 다발을 선물로 받았어요.
examples.en: I received a bunch of yellow daffodils as a gift.
I planted daffodil bulbs in a pot in the fall.

examples.ko: 꽃집에서 수선화를 사다가 책상에 꽂아 뒀어요.
examples.en: I bought daffodils at the flower shop and put them in a vase on my desk.

examples.ko: 제주도에는 수선화가 일찍 피어서 구경하러 갔어요.
examples.en: Daffodils bloom early on Jeju Island, so I went to see them.

examples.ko: 이 수선화 향기가 방 안에 가득해요.
examples.en: The scent of these daffodils fills the whole room.

explain: 봄꽃 이야기를 할 때 개나리, 튤립과 함께 자주 나와요. 물 '水(수)'와 신선 '仙(선)'이 들어간 꽃 이름이라 '옷을 고치는 수선'과는 관계가 없어요.

phrases.example: 수선화 한 송이를 책상 위에 놓았어요.
phrases.en: I put a single daffodil on my desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃을 셀 때는 '송이'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counting word for flowers is '송이'.

phrases.en: I planted daffodils in a flowerpot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃을 키우려고 땅이나 화분에 넣을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when planting flowers in the ground or a pot.

phrases.en: The daffodils are in full bloom in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 완전히 열린 모습을 '활짝'으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '활짝' describes flowers fully open.

explain_en: It often appears in talk about spring flowers, along with '개나리' (forsythia) and '튤립' (tulip). It is a flower name and has nothing to do with '수선', meaning clothing alterations.

examples.en: A rooster crowed loudly at dawn.
Roosters are bigger than hens.
We raise a rooster in the yard.
A rooster climbed onto the roof.
I saw a rooster and hens at the farm.
Try waking up early like a rooster.

explain: 수탉은 수컷 닭이고 반대말은 '암탉'이에요. 암수를 가리지 않거나 고기를 말할 때는 그냥 '닭'이라고 해요. 닭의 울음소리는 '꼬끼오'라고 표현해요.

phrases.en: A rooster crows every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수탉의 가장 대표적인 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical image of a rooster.

phrases.en: A rooster and hens live together on the farm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '암탉'과 함께 암수를 구분해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the opposite word '암탉' to tell the sexes apart.

phrases.en: The rooster's crow woke me up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수탉이 우는 소리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the sound a rooster makes.

explain_en: 수탉 is a male chicken and its opposite is 암탉. When sex doesn't matter, or when speaking of the meat, people just say 닭. A rooster's crow is written as 꼬끼오.

examples.en: Santa Claus rides a sleigh pulled by reindeer.
Reindeer live in cold northern regions.
I saw a reindeer in person in Finland.
A reindeer has large antlers on its head.
The child drew a reindeer on the Christmas card.

examples.ko: 눈 덮인 숲에서 순록 떼가 걸어가고 있어요.
examples.en: A herd of reindeer is walking through the snowy forest.

explain: '순록'은 추운 지방에 사는 사슴이에요. 한국 사람들은 크리스마스 이야기 때문에 '루돌프'라는 이름과 함께 떠올려요. 한국의 산에서 보는 '사슴'과는 다른 동물이에요.

phrases.example: 순록이 끄는 썰매를 타 보고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to ride a sleigh pulled by reindeer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크리스마스 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The expression that appears most often in Christmas stories.

phrases.en: A herd of reindeer is passing over the snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 마리가 함께 다닐 때 '떼'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '떼' when many of them move together.

phrases.en: People in the northern regions raise reindeer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물을 키울 때 '기르다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '기르다' when raising animals.

explain_en: '순록' is a deer that lives in cold regions. Because of the Christmas story, Koreans associate it with the name '루돌프'. It is different from the '사슴' seen in Korean mountains.

examples.en: Could there be life that came from outer space?

examples.ko: 그 영화는 외계 생명체와 친구가 되는 이야기예요.
examples.en: That movie is about becoming friends with an alien.
Scientists are searching for planets outside our solar system.
My younger brother believes aliens really exist.
The news said they heard a signal from outer space.
Children love stories about aliens.

explain: 외계는 지구 밖의 세계라는 뜻이라서 보통 '외계인', '외계 생명체'처럼 붙어서 나와요. '외계에서 온'처럼 단독으로도 쓰지만 합친 말이 더 많아요. 같이 알아 둘 말로 '우주'가 있어요.

phrases.en: A cute alien appears in that movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지구 밖에서 온 존재를 가리키는 가장 흔한 합친 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common compound word for a being from outside Earth.

phrases.en: Scientists discovered a new exoplanet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우리 태양계 밖의 행성을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for planets outside our solar system.

phrases.en: There is still a lot we don't know about space.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외계보다 넓은 뜻으로, 지구 밖 전체 공간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 외계, it refers to all the space beyond Earth.

explain_en: Realm beyond Earth or outside; sci-fi and space talk (외계인) 외계 is the world outside Earth, and usually appears in compounds like 외계인 (alien) and 외계 생명체 (alien life form). It can stand alone, as in '외계에서 온', but compounds are more common. 우주 (universe) is a related word.
